title.label: Would be a lot better with more intelligent features to reduce cognitive overload.

content.label:
Been a Calm user for years. Recently saw an ad on Instagram that took me to quiz.calm.com. Had me answer a few dozen questions. I figured maybe Calm had a new feature to build a custom plan for me so I don’t just keep picking the same old meditations. Nope. It was just a marketing bait and switch. There’s not even a feature to build a plan based on the 25 questions it just asked me. Just wanted me to put in my credit card and subscribe (spoiler… I’m already a subscriber). Incredibly frustrating. 

So here’s the new feature you should build. Ask me those 25 questions from your quiz, but then build me a plan automatically based on it. When I open the app, I don’t want to have to go digging for the meditation I want. That could take minutes staring at a screen adding more cognitive overload to my life. Instead, create a plan for me and then allow me to tweak it over time. THAT would be valuable. THAT would keep me as a subscriber. I’ve found the app less and less useful over time and am probably going to unsubscribe, but that would help change it around for me.

Do I still have anxiety and depression YES YES  it will never go away but there is a much clearer understanding of how meditation helps me deal with everyday life.

title.label: Daily Jay, Tamara and EMDR so good

content.label: I listen to the Daily Jay every day as I brew my coffee and the wisdom is SO GREAT. The wisdom in Tamara's daily meditations is so good too, though I still am not great at meditating, but I will continue to try. The EMDR is EXCELLENT for my ADHD when I'm feeling overwhelmed by the seemingly millions of tasks that hit me all at once to the point of paralysis. Or when I have super high anxiety, especially if I wake up with it, i can easily pop in my AirPods and feel the ability to take a really good deep breath (which I'm unable to do in high anxiety situations). Oh! And the sleep stories are great when my usual tricks won't work, but honestly I always forget about those. Of my four favorite tools in the app, the EMDR tracks feel the most life-saving, and Daily Jay is my favorite

title.label: Recent update broke soundscapes automatically looping.

content.label: The soundscapes now no longer autoplay and loop back on themselves and instead will play another unrelated soundscape or session that’s next in the recently played list once the track is finished. One second I’m asleep to the sound of a thunderstorm, the next I’m sitting in a sandstorm on Arrakis. I've had the app for a while as I got it through work. I didn't use it at all - I figured I knew enough about mindfulness and meditation. Then was hospitalized and  recovering from - new to me - severe neurological problems that were so bad I could no longer walk.
While in an excellent rehab hospital, one of the very first doctors that I saw asked if I was familiar with mindfulness and meditation. I said yes, but it's not something I've practicing lately. His first prescription for me was for me to return to practicing those things starting that evening, even if it was as little as five minutes. I remembered I had the Calm app and figured I should check it out as it was one of the tools he mentioned. It's been a lifesaver! I love it. I love the variety and I love all the daily check-ins. I've been using it daily for the last couple of months, and it's been so helpful - a life saver! Give it a chance - you may find a whole new set of tools ❤️

I subscribed to Calm as a support for developing healthier sleep habits. But soon discovered that there’s a wide and growing variety of resources for finding “calm” at any time. I especially like the breathing tool. I like it so much, I upgraded to the family plan and have shared with two siblings!
